pk.context: 1 mcg/kg intravenous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colourless solution in a single-dose glass bottle

clues.kinetics: Given intravenously, it is about 94% bound to plasma protein. Almost all of it is biotransformed, through glucuronidation and cytochrome P450 metabolism.
clues.substance: A hydrochloride salt, with a molecular weight of 200.28 for the active base.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in 200 mcg and 400 mcg sizes at 4 mcg per mL, infused for no more than 24 hours.
clues.safety: No boxed warning, and no contraindications are listed. Hypotension, bradycardia and dry mouth are the most common reactions in adults.
clues.indication: Sedation of intubated adults in intensive care, and of non-intubated adults and children before or during procedures.
clues.mechanism: A relatively selective, centrally acting alpha-2 agonist; at high doses, alpha-1 activity also appears.

tell: A 6-minute distribution half-life and a 2-hour terminal half-life set this alpha-2 agonist apart.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Initiate at one mcg/kg over 10 minutes
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: is approximately 2 hours and clearance is estimated to be approximately 39 L/h
